$comment: Canonical prose version: Rules/03_VALIDATION.md. Remote and folder manifests are validated by two separate functions in Infrastructure/MetadataSync/metadata-sync-service/server.js: validateRemoteToolManifest() and validateManifestSchema(). If this file and server.js ever disagree, server.js is authoritative — see Rules/INDEX.md.
title: SubverseLab Product Manifest

remoteManifest.$comment: source_type: "remote". Remote AI tools must never use the folder schema below.

slug.description: Unique product identifier; used as the Firestore document ID

tool_url.description: The tool's real, independently-deployed URL. Internal registration metadata only — never the public launch URL, never fetched from for manifest/guide/cover content. Checked for SSRF safety because it is rendered in an iframe on the live site.

iframe_compatible.description: Certification metadata, not a live check: what whoever registered the product observed by inspecting the tool's actual X-Frame-Options/CSP headers. MetadataSync never probes this automatically. Drives whether the Tool Room renders the tool in an iframe or falls back to an external-open state.

level.description: SubverseLab route/UI access gating on /tools/:slug only. Not a hard security boundary on deployment.tool_url — no auth/token is forwarded across the origin boundary into the tool. Real access control, if needed, is the tool's own responsibility.

label.description: Optional human-readable button text. Frontend falls back to a default label when absent.

url.description: Must NOT be present on a 'launch' action — the public launch URL is always /tools/:slug, derived from slug, never stored here or anywhere else.

folderManifest.$comment: source_type: "folder". Unchanged by the remote-tool architecture.

cover_path.description: Relative path inside the uploaded ZIP — no '..' segments, no absolute paths.

guide_path.description: Relative path inside the uploaded ZIP — no '..' segments, no absolute paths.

content_path.description: Relative path inside the uploaded ZIP — no '..' segments, no absolute paths.
